customer_it_admin: Hey, our private deployment in the on-prem bastion is failing to reach Redwood API from the app pods. Getting repeated 502/504 and occasional TLS errors.

maria_support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the curl/openssl output? Which mode: Private (VPC) or Dedicated? Any proxy in front?

customer_it_admin: Private/VPC. Yes, outbound goes via corporate HTTP proxy (explicit proxy) and they do TLS inspect. App uses env http_proxy/https_proxy set to proxy.corp:8080. Errors from app logs: `error: tls: handshake failure` then `401 unauthorized` sometimes. Also some requests show `502 Bad Gateway` from the proxy.

alex.s: Quick ask: can you run these from the bastion where the pod egress is NATed? 1) `curl -v --proxy http://proxy.corp:8080 https://api.redwood.run/v1/health` 2) `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.run:443 -servername api.redwood.run -showcerts`

customer_it_admin: Ran them. curl shows `Connected to proxy.corp` then `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway`. openssl shows a cert issued by corp-inspect-ca and subject CN=proxy-inspect.local. So proxy is doing MITM.

maria_support: That points to TLS inspection. Our client libraries expect to see Redwood cert and use SNI for routing. When MITM rewrites certs or rewrites SNI to the cached hostname, it can break token binding or backend routing. Two options: 1) configure proxy to allow TLS passthrough for `api.redwood.run` (CONNECT with 443, no inspect), or 2) install the corporate inspect CA into the host/container trust store AND ensure SNI is preserved. Which proxy appliance (Palo Alto, Bluecoat, F5)?

customer_it_admin: Palo Alto. We can't exempt everything; compliance wants inspection for most domains. Is there a minimal allowlist we can do?

alex.s: Yes — you can allow TLS passthrough for just `api.redwood.run` and `*.redwood.run` FQDNs. If not possible, add the corp-inspect CA to the runtime trust store used by your app (JVM cacerts / system CA). Also ensure forward DNS resolves to the public IPs, not internal split-horizon that points to a private hop.

josh_p: Also check firewall egress: many customers block destination IPs and only allow proxy by IP/port. Our hosted API IP range (published in console) needs to be allowed for outbound 443. Blocking outbound port 853 (DoT) can break DNS-over-TLS queries to public resolvers used by the proxy.

customer_it_admin: We had an allowlist by IPs but use a corporate DNS that returns internal A for `api.redwood.run` (split-horizon). That maps to private mgmt boxes which drop CONNECT. So DNS is the culprit too.

maria_support: Repro steps we recommend to validate: 1) From bastion: `dig +short api.redwood.run @1.1.1.1` and compare to internal resolve. 2) `curl -v --proxy http://proxy.corp:8080 --header 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' https://api.redwood.run/v1/models` 3) `openssl s_client -connect <resolved_ip>:443 -servername api.redwood.run` — check cert CN. 4) If you see corp-inspect CA, either add CA to runtime or request passthrough.

customer_it_admin: We tried adding corp CA to the container base image trust and still get 502 spikes. Taking a pcap shows proxy injecting a reset when backend returns 403 during auth exchange.

alex.s: That sounds like proxy transforming bodies or blocking token refresh endpoints. Confirm POST payloads/paths are allowed. Also check for Content-Length rewrite and keepalive settings. If you can, enable proxy logs for CONNECT sessions for `api.redwood.run` and share redacted logs.

eng-oncall-bot: Support ticket created #SUP-20260317-8719 — assigned to eng-oncall.

maria_support: For a short-term mitigation, you can route Redwood API egress through a dedicated outbound NAT egress host that bypasses the corporate proxy (if policy allows), or use a secure egress gateway with TLS passthrough to preserve SNI and certs. Long-term: request small proxy policy change to allow passthrough for our domains.

customer_it_admin: Ok will raise change with infra team and test bypass route. We'll share proxy logs and traceroute.

maria_support: Great — ping us with logs. If passthrough can't be approved, we'll provide exact CA fingerprint steps and a config checklist for JVM/pip/node to trust corp-inspect CA and preserve Authorization header through proxy.

customer_it_admin: Thanks all. I'll update once infra responds.
